or with their consent abstract rhizopus microsporus is an opportunistic fungal pathogen and a prominent etiological agent of mucormycosis a life threatening invasive fungal infection in this study we investigated the role of choc a gene encoding a putative phospholipid methyltransferase involved in phosphatidylcholine pc biosynthesis through the bremer greenberg pathway deletion of choc using crispr cas9 led to severe defects in growth and asexual development which persisted even at 37 c a temperature relevant to host infection supplementation with choline or its precursor pdea restored growth confirming the importance of choc in maintaining pc levels lipidomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed broad disruptions in pc and phosphatidylethanolamine pe levels glycerol 3 phosphate and fatty acid metabolism endoplasmic reticulum er stress responses and vesicle trafficking notably δchoc mutants exhibited reduced melanin and chitin content while ergosterol levels remained unaffected indicating specific impairment in cell envelope assembly in a murine infection model the δchoc mutant showed attenuated virulence linking lipid imbalance to impaired host adaptation together these findings highlight choc as a key regulator of membrane homeostasis and fungal pathogenicity as the methylation dependent pc synthesis pathway is barely present in human tissues choc represents a promising target for selective antifungal therapies keywords rhizopus microsporus phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis choc bremer greenberg pathway virulence mucormycosis status released display pdf yes is olf no is manuscript no is preprint no is journal matter no is scanned no is retracted no received 2025 sep 26 accepted 2026 mar 29 collection date 2026 introduction rhizopus microsporus is a filamentous basal fungus belonging to the subdivision mucoromycotina and the order mucorales 1 it is recognized as a model organism for studying symbiotic interactions between bacteria and fungi 2 4 and has notable industrial applications such as the production of enzymes and fermented foods 5 6 however r microsporus is also one of the primary opportunistic pathogens responsible for mucormycosis 7 an invasive infection characterized by blood vessel invasion thrombosis and tissue necrosis these features favor fungal dissemination throughout the host 8 resulting in high mortality rates that can reach up to 90 in cases where the infection becomes systemic because of this severity the disease has been colloquially termed black fungus 9 11 species of rhizopus along with mucor and lichtheimia account for approximately 90 of mucormycosis cases 11 12 while this disease mainly affects individuals with diabetes or immunosuppression treated with corticosteroids 13 it can also occur in otherwise healthy individuals following traumatic inoculation 14 this became particularly evident during the second wave of the covid 19 pandemic in asian countries especially in india where a significant increase in post covid 19 mucormycosis cases was reported 14 15 recently new molecular and genetic strategies based on the crispr cas9 system have been developed to manipulate the genome of r microsporus 16 making it the only mucoral pathogen currently available for genetic modification these tools enable the study of essential components for mucoralean fungal development positioning r microsporus as an ideal model for research and the development of specific and effective antifungal therapies against mucormycosis lipids are a fundamental class of biomolecules essential for life notable for their structural and functional diversity across biological systems 17 in 2005 the international lipid classification and nomenclature committee categorized lipids into eight major categories fatty acids fa glycerolipids gl glycerophospholipids gp sphingolipids sl sterol lipids st prenol lipids pr saccharolipids sl and polyketides pk 18 with fa gp sl and st being the most common lipid classes in cell membranes 19 20 among glycerophospholipids phosphatidylcholine pc is the most abundant component of cell membranes playing a wide variety of molecular roles furse de kroon 2015 papangelis ulven 2022 21 22 there are two main pathways for pc biosynthesis i the kennedy pathway and ii the bremer greenberg pathway or methylation pathway in mammals except hepatocytes nematodes plants and malaria parasites the kennedy pathway is the predominant route for pc synthesis 23 26 in contrast both pathways contribute to pc biosynthesis in fungi and in human hepatocytes although in the latter the methylation pathway accounts for only 30 of pc production 19 27 28 in saccharomyces cerevisiae the bremer greenberg pathway begins with serine which is decarboxylated to form phosphatidylserine this intermediate is then converted into pc through three sequential methylation steps using s adenosyl l methionine as the methyl group donor the first reaction is catalyzed by cho2 a class ii phospholipid methyltransferase plmt whereas the subsequent two methylation steps are carried out by opi3 a class i plmt 12 20 28 conversely the kennedy pathway is initiated with choline which is phosphorylated and then conjugated with cytidine triphosphate ctp to facilitate its incorporation at the sn 3 position of the glycerol backbone 29 additionally the cdp dag route which originates from glycerol 3 phosphate g3p generates precursors shared by both biosynthetic pathways 30 31 figure 1 a figure 1 a schematic representation of the phosphatidylcholine pc biosynthesis the arrive 2 0 guidelines data analysis all experiments were randomized and the investigators performing the quantifications were blinded to the experimental conditions statistical analyses were conducted using graphpad prism version 8 0 1 graphpad software ca usa data were analyzed by two way analysis of variance two way anova followed by turkey s multiple comparisons test to evaluate the effects of two independent variables and their interaction or one way anove followed by turkey s multiple comparisons test to evaluate the effects of just one independent variable a p value 0 05 was considered statistically significant data are presented as mean standard deviation sd unless otherwise specified discussion in this study we characterized the role of choc which encodes a putative phospholipid methyltransferase in the filamentous fungus r microsporus deletion of choc resulted in pronounced defects in vegetative growth and sporulation in both solid and liquid media figure 2 a c d underscoring the importance of phosphatidylcholine pc biosynthesis for normal fungal development supplementation with choline or its precursor phosphodimethylethanolamine pdea restored normal growth confirming that the observed phenotypes stem from impaired pc production similar growth defects associated with disruptions in phospholipid methylation have been reported in other fungi although the extent of phenotypic recovery varies across species 20 56 in a fumigatus and a nidulans the phenotype is partially restored after four days of growth suggesting some compensation by the kennedy pathway or cdp dag pathway 20 in contrast no recovery is seen in r microsporus p microsporus or m robertsii indicating that choc dependent pc biosynthesis is essential in these species 12 34 these findings reinforce our conclusion that the contribution of the bremer greenberg pathway and the functional relevance of choc varies across the fungal kingdom interestingly this phenotype is not restricted to a specific temperature as previously characterized but is also evident at 37 c a temperature highly relevant in the context of host pathogen interactions the inability of the mutant to grow properly at host temperature suggests that choc dependent pc biosynthesis may be critical not only for environmental adaptation but also for fungal pathogenicity asexual development and cellular function in r microsporus surprisingly no significant differences were observed in the r microsporus δ choc mutant when grown in the presence of congo red compared to the control condition without the dye figure 2 b this contrasts with a fumigatus where choc mutants display clear hypersensitivity to congo red 20 in r microsporus the mutant already exhibits marked growth defects under normal conditions suggesting that the cell wall is sufficiently compromised such that additional stress from congo red has little or no additive effect supporting this quantification of cell wall components revealed a significant reduction in chitin content in δ choc strains whereas ergosterol levels remained unchanged relative to the wild type um6 figure 3 b c this selective depletion of chitin indicates that choc disruption affects specific aspects of wall biosynthesis likely through indirect effects on membrane organization vesicle trafficking or lipid mediated regulation of cell wall enzymes consistent with the quantitative measurements calcofluor white staining revealed a clear reduction in chitin associated fluorescence in the δ choc mutant under congo red stress figure 3 d e f g h i providing direct visual evidence of altered chitin distribution importantly supplementation with choline restored the calcofluor staining pattern supporting the idea that impaired endogenous phosphatidylcholine biosynthesis underlies the observed cell wall defects similar findings have been reported in candida albicans where disruption of phospholipid homeostasis leads to defective chitin deposition without altering ergosterol levels 57 as pc does not directly form part of the cell wall its role is most likely mediated through its influence on intracellular signaling and membrane dynamics 19 58 consistent with this transcriptomic analysis in the δ choc mutant revealed enrichment of a go term related to chitin deacetylase activity figure 4 c suggesting ongoing remodeling of the cell wall structure under conditions of lipid imbalance these results reinforce the role of choc in maintaining cell wall integrity and highlight species specific differences in compensatory responses to envelope stress transcriptomic analysis of the δ choc mutant reveals a coordinated disruption of membrane associated systems and core metabolic pathways underscoring the central role of pc biosynthesis in maintaining intracellular homeostasis in r microsporus gene enrichment patterns highlight the impact of choc deletion on multiple fronts beginning with vesicle trafficking between the er and golgi apparatus which are the primary sites of pc synthesis 19 specifically the differential expression of genes involved in copi and copii vesicle coat formation and intra golgi vesicle mediated transport suggests that pc is essential for vesicle budding cargo sorting and membrane curvature all of which are critical for maintaining secretory pathway integrity 59 60 in addition functional enrichment in protein disulfide isomerase activity chaperone binding and structural molecule activity indicates potential er stress 61 62 also found in a fumigatus 20 importantly choc deletion also impacted g3p metabolism particularly among mutant dependent genes influenced by temperature g3p serves as a key metabolic hub that connects glycolysis lipid biosynthesis via the kennedy and bremer greenberg pathways and redox regulation 19 63 altered regulation of g3p related genes suggests a metabolic shift to compensate for disrupted pc biosynthesis possibly through the redirection of carbon flux or alternative lipid remodeling strategies 63 64 this aligns with the enrichment of multiple fatty acid coa ligase genes of varying chain length specificity indicating broad reprogramming of fatty acid activation and routing 65 these results position choc as a key integrator of phospholipid synthesis with intracellular organization suggesting that pc is not only a structural lipid but also a regulator of organelle function and cellular adaptability under environmental stress transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses together revealed that choc plays a central and non redundant role in pc biosynthesis in r microsporus in δ choc mutants we observed transcriptional upregulation of cho2 pct1 and ept1 cpt1 paralogs figure 3 a genes associated with the kennedy pathway and early methylation steps suggesting that the cell attempts to redirect lipid metabolism toward pc synthesis via alternative routes however in the absence of choc which catalyzes the final methylation step this compensatory response is ineffective as a result pe is consumed but pc is not produced efficiently leading to a reduction in both pe and pc levels as confirmed by neutral loss scan data figure 4 e f interestingly in the wild type strain cho2 expression remains unchanged between 30 c and 37 c and pe levels are similarly stable across temperatures in contrast choc expression is specifically downregulated at 37 c a pattern that aligns with a mild decrease in pc content suggesting that r microsporus actively reduces choc expression under host like conditions possibly as a strategy to increase membrane fluidity during infection 66 however in the δ choc background this regulation is completely lost resulting in persistent disruption of lipid balance and inability to adapt membrane composition to temperature shifts importantly our data demonstrated that although the kennedy pathway is transcriptionally active it is insufficient to compensate for the loss of choc in line with this total pc levels dropped more than 21 fold at 30 c and 8 fold at 37 c in the δ choc mutant compared to wild type figure 5 e f these findings highlight that in r microsporus the bremer greenberg pathway is not only essential but also the dominant route for pc synthesis under the tested conditions acting in collaboration with but functionally outweighing the kennedy pathway the attenuated virulence observed in the δ choc mutant supports a functional link between phospholipid metabolism and pathogenicity in r microsporus although all infected mice ultimately succumbed the delayed mortality indicates that loss of choc compromises key physiological processes required for efficient host invasion and progression of infection similar connections between lipid metabolic pathways and fungal virulence have been described in multiple pathogenic fungi including c albicans a fumigatus and m robertsii where mutations affecting phospholipid biosynthesis impair growth cell wall integrity and pathogenicity 20 34 55 one contributing factor is the marked reduction in melanin production observed in δchoc strains melanin is a well established virulence factor that protects fungi from oxidative stress phagocytosis and antimicrobial compounds 67 similar impairments have been reported in melanin deficient mutants of a fumigatus and r delemar which show reduced survival in immune cells and decreased virulence 68 69 given that choc affects membrane lipid composition these defects may arise from altered vesicular trafficking of melanogenic enzymes or intermediates this notion is supported by our transcriptomic data which revealed disruptions in genes involved in vesicle formation and transport reinforcing the idea that phosphatidylcholine is crucial for proper trafficking and secretion processes targeting lipid metabolism has emerged as a promising antifungal strategy particularly for pathogens that exhibit intrinsic resistance to current drug classes recent reviews highlight fungal lipid biosynthesis pathways as attractive targets for antifungal drug development and for potentiating existing therapies 70 71 additionally a growing body of work underscores the importance of understanding fungal lipid biology for the discovery of novel antifungal targets 72 in this context inhibition of choc may represent a strategy to weaken fungal fitness and pathogenic potential either as a standalone approach or in combination with current antifungals rather than acting as a fungicidal target on its own finally given the substantial challenges associated with mucormycosis research including limitations in histopathological resolution and host pathogen modeling 73 the identification of molecular targets that simultaneously affect multiple virulence associated processes is of particular interest while further studies will be required to assess druggability specificity and in vivo efficacy our findings position choc as a promising candidate for future antifungal development efforts aimed at expanding the currently limited therapeutic arsenal against mucormycosis in summary c hoc is a central regulator of pc biosynthesis in r microsporus and its disruption leads to widespread metabolic and cellular defects these include reduced pc and pe levels altered glycerol 3 phosphate and fatty acid metabolism er stress impaired vesicle trafficking and compromised cell wall remodeling the mutant also showed reduced melanin and chitin content suggesting defects in membrane dependent secretion and envelope assembly collectively these alterations impair growth sporulation and virulence under host like conditions as r microsporus is one of the main causative agents of mucormycosis the functional conservation of choc in filamentous fungi and the limited role of the phospholipid methylation pathway in mammals restricted mainly to hepatocytes and contributing only 30 of total pc synthesis 19 choc emerges as a selective
